mcqs.q: The PRINCIPAL (most predominant) cell type of the periodontal ligament is the:
mcqs.explain: The principal cell type of the PDL is the fibroblast (with macrophages also predominant); the principal intercellular substance is collagen.

mcqs.q: The principal intercellular substance of the PDL is:
mcqs.explain: Collagen is the principal intercellular substance of the PDL, organized into the principal fibre bundles.

mcqs.q: Clusters of epithelial cells identified within the PDL on a slide are the:
mcqs.explain: The epithelial rests of Malassez appear as isolated clusters or strands of epithelial cells in the PDL (remnants of Hertwig's root sheath).

mcqs.q: To orient a PDL slide, the ligament lies between the:
opts: Cementum (tooth side) and the alveolar bone
mcqs.explain: The PDL occupies the space between the root cementum and the alveolar bone.

mcqs.q: The principal fibre groups anchor the tooth to bone. Which group is the LARGEST?
mcqs.explain: The oblique fibres are the largest group, running from cementum coronally up to the bone.

mcqs.q: The fibres running from the cervical cementum down to the bony crest are the:
mcqs.explain: Alveolar crest fibres extend from the cervical cementum (below the junctional epithelium) to the alveolar bone crest.

mcqs.q: Fibres running at right angles to the long axis of the tooth are the:
mcqs.explain: Horizontal fibres run at right angles to the long axis, from cementum to alveolar bone.

mcqs.q: The oblique fibres run from the cementum:
opts: Coronally (upward) to the bone, bearing chewing load
mcqs.explain: Oblique fibres run from the cementum in a coronal direction up to the bone, bearing the brunt of vertical chewing forces.

mcqs.q: The fibres that radiate at the root tip are the:
mcqs.explain: Apical fibres radiate from the cementum to the bone at the apical region of the socket.

opts: In the furcation area of multirooted teeth
At the apex of single-rooted teeth
mcqs.explain: Interradicular fibres fan out from cementum to bone in the furcation areas of multirooted teeth.

mcqs.q: Sharpey's fibres are the fibre ends embedded in:
opts: Cementum on one side and alveolar bone on the other
mcqs.explain: Sharpey's fibres are the mineralized terminal ends of the principal fibres, embedded in cementum and in alveolar bone.

mcqs.q: Besides fibroblasts, the other predominant cell type listed in the PDL is the:
mcqs.explain: Fibroblasts and macrophages are the most predominant cells found within the PDL.

mcqs.q: The epithelial rests of Malassez are remnants of:
mcqs.explain: The rests of Malassez are remnants of Hertwig's epithelial root sheath that persist in the PDL.

mcqs.q: On the malassez slide, the tooth-side mineralized tissue adjacent to the PDL is labelled:
mcqs.explain: On that slide the PDL borders acellular cementum, which overlies the root dentin; the rests of Malassez lie within the ligament.

mcqs.q: Which sequence correctly lists structures from the tooth outward?
mcqs.explain: From the tooth outward: dentin, then cementum, then the PDL, then the alveolar bone.

mcqs.q: The principal fibres function mainly to:
opts: Anchor the tooth to the bone
mcqs.explain: The principal fibres are groups of collagen fibres that anchor the tooth to the alveolar bone.

saqs.q: Name the principal cell and intercellular substance of the PDL.
saqs.a: Principal cell = fibroblast (with macrophages); principal intercellular substance = collagen.

saqs.q: List the principal fibre groups seen on a PDL slide.
saqs.a: Alveolar crest, horizontal, oblique (largest), apical, and interradicular fibres (plus transseptal between teeth).

saqs.q: How do you identify oblique fibres and why are they important?
saqs.a: They run from cementum coronally up to bone and are the largest group, bearing vertical chewing load.
The mineralized terminal ends of the principal fibres, embedded in cementum and alveolar bone.

saqs.q: What are the rests of Malassez and where are they seen?
saqs.a: Clusters/strands of epithelial cells within the PDL — remnants of Hertwig's root sheath.
